solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Caterer left one to have in meal

indicators.note: the meal is told to have the other letters inside it, so they go within its letters

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A caterer leaves one guest to be fed at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer provides food and drink, so is a provider of goods to customers.

clue.text: Raised a second order, for example, for pastry snack

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means written upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the OM is the Order of Merit
as can mean for example, as in 'trees, as oak and ash'

explanation.surface: Someone places a second order, for instance, for a pastry snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' in a down clue reads upwards: ASOMAS from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a fried triangular pastry filled with spiced vegetables or meat, eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Recognised border raider one might catch abroad

indicators.note: the ear catches a word that sounds like the raider's name

parts.note: the Picts raided across the northern border of Roman Britain
out can mean away from home, overseas

explanation.surface: A raider from the border was spotted by someone who could catch him overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The Picts were an ancient people of Scotland who raided Roman Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To single something out from a crowd is to identify it, a synonym for recognising.

clue.text: Appearing as card game champion

parts.note: loo is an old card game
a king is the best, the champion, as in 'king of the hill'

explanation.surface: Someone comes across as the best at a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO also means toilet in Britain, but here it is a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking can mean seeming, as in 'looking tired', so it matches appearing.

clue.text: First of exceptional leads for acting dame

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the vans are the leading parts, as in the vanguard

explanation.surface: An exceptional actress plays the leading roles.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Edith Evans was a celebrated English stage and film actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Evans was a British actress made a Dame of the British Empire, so an acting dame.

clue.text: Mayonnaise a lad dropped: that's so funny

indicators.note: the words 'a lad' are dropped, so those letters leave the dressing's name

parts.note: salad cream is a British bottled dressing, a cheaper cousin of mayonnaise
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds it hilarious that a boy dropped the mayonnaise.
explanation.walkthrough: SALAD CREAM is a tangy British bottled dressing, loosely equated with mayonnaise here. Taking out A LAD leaves S + CREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hilarious is informally called a scream, so the phrase stands for an uproariously funny thing.

clue.text: Islanders about to sunbathe in empty coves

indicators.note: the letters go inside the emptied word
empty coves keep only their outside letters

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to tan is to sunbathe

explanation.surface: Islanders sunbathe in quiet coves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here is a synonym, not an anagram signal, and 'empty' keeps only the outside letters of the bays.
explanation.definitionFit: Cretans are people of Crete, the largest of the Greek islands.

clue.text: Leave boat, half submerged by water in Devon

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece sits beneath the other, as if under the water

parts.note: the Exe is a river running through Devon

indicators.note: only one half of the word boat is kept, its second two letters

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a boat half sunk in a Devon river.
explanation.walkthrough: An EXEAT is the permission given at British boarding schools and colleges for a pupil to be absent.
explanation.definitionFit: An exeat is formal permission to be absent, as leave is for a soldier.

clue.text: Looked after the sappers recruited by government department once

indicators.note: the department takes the other letters into itself, as a recruiting body would

parts.note: MoD is the Ministry of Defence
RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers

explanation.surface: The army engineers joined by a ministry were cared for.
explanation.definitionFit: To mother someone is to nurture and protect them, caring like a parent.

clue.text: Relative I don't like that is involved in dodgy trade

indicators.note: the exclamation becomes involved in, enclosed by, the other letters
dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone disapproves of a relative caught up in shady business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' shuffles the business word to give DATER, and the grunt of disgust sits inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter is a female child, one kind of family relation.

clue.text: 007's boss in charge of Italian spy will keep me in tight control

parts.note: M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories
a Roman is an Italian from Rome

indicators.note: the spy will keep the next word held inside

parts.note: an agent is a spy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bond's chief, running an Italian spy, keeps him on a short leash.
explanation.definitionFit: Micromanaging is supervising every small detail of others' work, an excessively close kind of oversight.

clue.text: Type that is wearing glasses

indicators.note: the glasses go round the other letters, as if worn on them

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone describes the type of person who wears glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' here means the eyewear goes on the outside, round the Latin abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a kind or sort, as in 'a rare species of optimist'.

clue.text: One receiving money from family member getting support of course

parts.note: gran is a grandmother
a tee supports the ball on a golf course

explanation.surface: Someone gets cash from a relative, backing them through college, of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally', but means on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A grantee is the recipient of a grant, a sum awarded for a purpose.

clue.text: Guess it's taken by one driving off

definitions.meaning: a wild attempt with little chance of being right

definitions.text: it's taken by one driving off
definitions.meaning: a golfer driving off the tee may play a big hit down the fairway

explanation.surface: A guess about what a departing driver takes with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving off' suggests leaving in a car; it is a golfer's opening stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: An unlikely guess is a speculative attempt, and in golf a big hit from the tee travels far.

clue.text: Dance with a tall, so-called Western hero

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
long can mean tall, as in long legs

explanation.surface: A cowboy hero dances with a tall partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Hopalong Cassidy was a cowboy hero of American films and TV; 'so-called' marks it as his nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopalong Cassidy was the nickname of a fictional cowboy of Western films and books.

clue.text: Woman resolved issue

indicators.note: resolved can mean broken up and recast, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman sorted out a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Susie is a female given name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: I may get in new order for artist?

definitions.text: I may get in new order for artist?

indicators.note: the letters for the pronoun get in among the other letters
the word artist is put into a new order, rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper says they may get in a fresh order for an artist customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new order for' shuffles the painter word to STATIR, and 'may get in' slips the numeral inside it. The whole clue is also the shopkeeper speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of paper, pens and art materials might restock supplies when an artist places an order.

clue.text: Dogs crowd round headless corpse

indicators.note: the crowd goes round the other letters

parts.note: a mass is a crowd

indicators.note: headless means losing the first letter

parts.note: stiff is slang for a corpse

explanation.surface: A pack of dogs and a crowd surround a beheaded body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' drops the first letter of the slang word for a body, and 'round' wraps the crowd about what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastiffs are large, powerful breeds of guard dog.

clue.text: Carrier of heavy loads in particular

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the following word

explanation.surface: A specific kind of heavy-goods carrier is being singled out.
explanation.walkthrough: An ARTIC is a British articulated lorry, a large truck with a separate cab.
explanation.definitionFit: An articulated lorry is a heavy goods vehicle that hauls big cargoes.

clue.text: North-facing parkland including terrain originally for farmer

indicators.note: in a down entry, facing north means reading upwards, so backwards
the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public park

indicators.note: originally means taking the first letter

explanation.surface: A farmer's land faces north, park and rough ground included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts the T and the clue's 'for' inside the park, and 'North-facing' reads RETFORC upwards. A croft is a small Scottish farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A crofter tends a croft, a small rented farm in the Scottish Highlands and Islands.

clue.text: South American training to race across Roman road

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: the race stretches across the road, so the road goes inside

parts.note: to run is to race
via is Latin for road, as in the Via Appia

explanation.surface: A South American athlete trains by racing along an old Roman road.
explanation.definitionFit: A Peruvian is a native of Peru, a country in South America.

clue.text: Old university in America when holiday starts is empty

indicators.note: the holiday starts the answer, coming first

parts.note: vac is short for vacation

indicators.note: the old university letters go inside America's

parts.note: US stands for United States

explanation.surface: An old American college is deserted when the holidays begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacuous means lacking content or thought, essentially blank or hollow.

clue.text: Ducks lose strength after eating some corn

indicators.note: the first word swallows the second, taking it inside

parts.note: to die away or die down is to lose strength
an ear of corn is a portion of it

explanation.surface: Ducks become weak after feeding on corn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ducks' is a British term of endearment ('ta, duck'), not birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal terms of affection for a loved one, used like 'darling'.

clue.text: Work planting hops, avoiding hard earth

indicators.note: the work plants the other letters inside it, as a gardener sets bulbs in soil

parts.note: toil is hard work

indicators.note: the word hops avoids, so loses, the letter for hard

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A farmhand plants hops while steering clear of solid ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding hard' drops the H from the brewing plant, and 'planting' sets what is left inside the word for work.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper layer of soil in a field or garden is the earth that plants grow in.

clue.text: Heathen commander invading borders of Pakistan

indicators.note: the commander invades, moving inside the edges
the borders are the outside letters of the word

parts.note: an aga is an Ottoman military commander

explanation.surface: An infidel commander invades Pakistan's frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: An aga was an Ottoman officer; 'borders of' keeps just the country's first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan is a heathen, someone outside the main world religions.

clue.text: Feeling retired priest is behind diplomacy

indicators.note: the priest comes behind, after, the word for diplomacy

parts.note: tact is diplomacy

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the priest's name is read backwards

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A sensitive clergyman has retired, though diplomacy remains behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns ELI to ILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile describes things perceived by touch, as in feeling something with the fingers.

clue.text: Awfully big day coming up for old poet

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: OS means outsize, a clothing label for very large sizes
Sat is short for Saturday

explanation.surface: A very big day is approaching for an old poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses OSSAT upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was a sixteenth-century Italian poet, author of Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: Those conferring about how to show resistance

indicators.note: about can mean around or turned round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: People in a meeting discuss how to resist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it rearranges the fifteen letters of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand up for your own position under pressure is a way of resisting, so the idiom names a method of standing firm.

clue.text: Divers dehydrate thus after open-air dip?

definitions.meaning: an old word meaning various or several
after a dip outdoors you might dry off in the sunshine

explanation.surface: Swimmers dry themselves in the sun after a swim outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like swimmers, but is the archaic adjective meaning various.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundry means various or miscellaneous, and to sun-dry is to dry by exposure to sunshine.

clue.text: Scone removed from wrapping, provide jam

indicators.note: the word scone is taken out of its wrapping, losing its outer letters

parts.note: to serve is to provide food

explanation.surface: Someone unwraps a scone and offers jam to go with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A conserve is a fruit preserve, a kind of jam with whole pieces of fruit.
